transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm really only here because everyone else keeps saying I'm way too thin and sick. I honestly don't see what the big deal is about my weight right now, but my coworkers and the doctors at the urgent care wouldn't let it go.
Do you ever feel like you lose control over your eating and consume a very large amount of food in a short period, or do you strictly restrict your food intake to maintain your current weight?

I definitely don't lose control; if anything, I strictly control what I eat. Most days I just have a coffee in the morning, maybe a banana or half a sandwich during my shift, and then some soup or a small salad at night. I do that because I really don't want to feel heavy or stuffed anymore.
Do you ever engage in episodes where you eat a large amount of food followed by self-induced vomiting, excessive exercise, or the use of laxatives to prevent weight gain?
No, I've never done anything like that. I don't eat large amounts of food at all, so I have no reason to throw up or use laxatives. I just try to keep my eating as minimal as possible.
When you look in the mirror or think about your body, do you perceive yourself as overweight despite what others tell you about your weight?

I don't see myself as too thin or sick at all; I just think I look fit and maybe a bit tired. If I let my weight creep back up, I feel like I'll become that sloppy, out-of-shape guy my ex used to nag about. Staying lean is the one thing that makes me feel like I'm doing something right, so I really think everyone is making a mountain out of a molehill.

Specifically, since the patient denies binge-eating or purging behaviors, F50.01 (Anorexia nervosa, restricting type) is the most precise ICD-10 classification.
